document.query: Summarize the state of nuclear fusion net-energy gain experiments since the NIF 2022 milestone, including ITER updates and private sector progress.
document.raw_markdown:
Following the historic December 2022 demonstration of net energy gain, the field of nuclear fusion research has seen both significant advancements and notable setbacks [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFNeaHyxX18iMCYOD3OEZ9KNTtk63QPKJCi-Or2wPFbryJfHffl99p3y48xUTXY5W1Ef6E9y9KyViL9KpRjdVHvu12-OeH9mPh_dsQwDEQYoyTmgRSpV1OSNqp8boKFkf1DpzyKADPwGFKBlg==). The National Ignition Facility (NIF) has repeatedly surpassed its initial breakthrough, while the international ITER project faces a revised and delayed timeline. Concurrently, the private sector is experiencing a surge in investment and technological progress, with several companies achieving key milestones [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHjzyAiBGqE40Cn5OvOQi-W3K3Vn-uPAEeWm3XT97-1byD7yLfvzxido5uNkHvif_-ifWe4HoMgxMXqADxVUKK9H7cnnwER0F8HgxFv66fNkWbGZH7GelgUT0IDSiJIxQdPsMVXAp0BKDAXTYvPxOJa2h833VPq00UlCy9MZVLcu1ogPyjQyNZvV0kA1nvdxIc=).

At Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, the NIF has continued to build on its 2022 success in inertial confinement fusion [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFBET4q8mPJJ_t6iHiFkyZvEyQzqVvtuCN-8rIgU9DCJCoQhQMu3A8cdw1tcCb5P3eh6vBudNC8zMWLiuxQh2j0xkDhq22aPbVS99V46YG1Tvn_WZBBvv89wYM93SuKucWdqXDflYlY_Ahz8FCkDdO6g-gD). In the initial experiment, 2.05 megajoules (MJ) of laser energy produced 3.15 MJ of fusion energy [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFMSDz7lXEx9Sw4ySCnFSGVkc1IN0cdaX6GqSnxHQuRIm0nw6wtQ25yy0R9o_to21cnBDXGZgTV2j2mzMUdUpgiyK24T3A1Q64AMEUzfqax00MMgW0Odh6xEjOlX1c_QWXu7sCx3VFbnSRb2hYwj2ZMvtTzUA==). Since then, NIF has achieved ignition multiple times with increasing energy yields [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQF7nQKzuuVay_J8j3f2BCjut4nOVeXkqgFvR1A3-j2itAhyG8JhS75WHN5caC28VgXJR1GUTN4AaZuzvGoOVrPEGlMQc0plFgo3b8LBMz4OThLK8M0ssTJL_tzunQ47IHITK4bxJsxME_Wrwjay0K8eZoKXWX0IrGiqwg33V0GXKyN7qZWXQw==) [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFMSDz7lXEx9Sw4ySCnFSGVkc1IN0cdaX6GqSnxHQuRIm0nw6wtQ25yy0R9o_to21cnBDXGZgTV2j2mzMUdUpgiyK24T3A1Q64AMEUzfqax00MMgW0Odh6xEjOlX1c_QWXu7sCx3VFbnSRb2hYwj2ZMvtTzUA==). Notably, a February 2024 experiment generated approximately 5.2 MJ of energy from a 2.2 MJ laser input [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHkpt8uuvlc0VrK_4WI_4wIyh7xFYtnJRPL_YUxCIlQGp_7ew-TPGXDb8VxNE7jVnIpxNgVCQxdazVVa1aeM6qkVia81n0DHsOEIyM82B8OQs0nfh4htblJBU6zhf3DlsADpeQ8czZwBWPxamH1zvJIFFoxWNRFQ1P3) [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQF7nQKzuuVay_J8j3f2BCjut4nOVeXkqgFvR1A3-j2itAhyG8JhS75WHN5caC28VgXJR1GUTN4AaZuzvGoOVrPEGlMQc0plFgo3b8LBMz4OThLK8M0ssTJL_tzunQ47IHITK4bxJsxME_Wrwjay0K8eZoKXWX0IrGiqwg33V0GXKyN7qZWXQw==). By April 2025, another experiment set a new record, producing 8.6 MJ of energy from 2.08 MJ delivered to the target, a more than fourfold gain [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQF7nQKzuuVay_J8j3f2BCjut4nOVeXkqgFvR1A3-j2itAhyG8JhS75WHN5caC28VgXJR1GUTN4AaZuzvGoOVrPEGlMQc0plFgo3b8LBMz4OThLK8M0ssTJL_tzunQ47IHITK4bxJsxME_Wrwjay0K8eZoKXWX0IrGiqwg33V0GXKyN7qZWXQw==) [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG7vUd52GQad_aRvX4w6bOWwMdxF4SYmHJvzjulfmud_LzpMpnItaCFmq5i7r4-hjzY7HUk_XxzsLuarAkXvy1FmDFc_vxgamAJy2dQavLuKe597vlHc89C3zwDnURx-aeKvENNhSh6cPd6MB1Pye8FqUdJj-pqUsNIVa-rnlJTQnqm0yqLn8_J4_meiaxoDdPWqP046S_Bh30Odxu7g1b-5C0YXOPPu1LZky0YLC0loRqrswHU7Ab5wvHq0AjhJv2btoPRR13yHditIL0TrA==) [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHhelDIp0MdXKs5A42AE-lzA1N16iY9CZcAvy8DsKYz_-vJm2lq9S7EsElP2dWTdAm2yTAEXFvrb0y1XXaz5qoIGvbgbkeayoAEpMqKiTYCoZG00k8l_h5owoIP1vGEkaqQe-TlzwTyLt3K838ra-VwMrpOGvyMuRY5qwYUUe2wPd3BOhvz5tBYmoHxnUeXbrUtX2-1hwDsLDgogvmxmUngz9uhiw==). These repeated successes demonstrate a growing understanding and control over the ignition process, a crucial step toward the prospect of inertial fusion energy [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEuVNZyzDgm7F3QMFCSeywrQNLGiy2MDv221SjeqBv9ncQSxBSnt4w-PEB1TaxuI1-4goFeIV-4bO41CvmwGMeO6Nzi_7IcRVbOwpHLxXZkyiTaa3YP75P_r3ZoxZMbY10ulpXYAT7olJZymb_TmK5BZaSTyO_1oWbMeA==). However, it is important to note that while these experiments have achieved scientific net energy gain (more energy out of the fuel pellet than laser energy delivered), they do not yet account for the total energy required to power the entire facility's laser system, which is significantly higher [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFBET4q8mPJJ_t6iHiFkyZvEyQzqVvtuCN-8rIgU9DCJCoQhQMu3A8cdw1tcCb5P3eh6vBudNC8zMWLiuxQh2j0xkDhq22aPbVS99V46YG1Tvn_WZBBvv89wYM93SuKucWdqXDflYlY_Ahz8FCkDdO6g-gD) [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHhelDIp0MdXKs5A42AE-lzA1N16iY9CZcAvy8DsKYz_-vJm2lq9S7EsElP2dWTdAm2yTAEXFvrb0y1XXaz5qoIGvbgbkeayoAEpMqKiTYCoZG00k8l_h5owoIP1vGEkaqQe-TlzwTyLt3K838ra-VwMrpOGvyMuRY5qwYUUe2wPd3BOhvz5tBYmoHxnUeXbrUtX2-1hwDsLDgogvmxmUngz9uhiw==).

In contrast to NIF's rapid experimental progress, the international ITER (International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor) project in France has encountered significant delays [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHFhZ1yEceYqDXSbiiWscWWNsAbNdodzwx3AY_WkQlA5QEO04II-yDu0PfgRZDGCFJqfa6Y3W3I5g0wtzYhYR9iZrCLEqaIhIkmSnC94phVMH8dx-OckLS93cqycR9EjYdUL2oK99ZjIM4j2yQ=). Originally slated for "first plasma" in 2025, the project's timeline has been substantially revised [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHvhqrB79sg2Z8vk5-7Ga5vMmOfamzrVLqne2NIKmGNsf-xzn3wI9vZ5dqtsO6U6IAO8FKNy28XV8HHHsZOEkyZ4tnvB7M9Hh-baJsiXjFZnpjBom6HqeIG5RU5UxiI0dqZH5BBI9Vkr5U7QwYFCRvqV6O1Zz9Z0cY9ttuJXt4aOkt-jHaNRMEFhLfwIDFbS5KG8Wb1P5tMN5rybDGpow==). The new schedule, announced in mid-2024, pushes the start of initial research operations to 2034, with deuterium-deuterium fusion experiments planned for 2035 and full deuterium-tritium operations, aimed at significant power generation, now expected in 2039 [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHFhZ1yEceYqDXSbiiWscWWNsAbNdodzwx3AY_WkQlA5QEO04II-yDu0PfgRZDGCFJqfa6Y3W3I5g0wtzYhYR9iZrCLEqaIhIkmSnC94phVMH8dx-OckLS93cqycR9EjYdUL2oK99ZjIM4j2yQ=) [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFPLamdfbmjkhhXUnPnd_byA-Vk8tWoPjD4viNzIeetGOf15NmJA1JsSzSvSgiuO7QdAPhrJElptGnpU-536EYbt8fIVASihFVixxqnMvMddUFfGyx6VwM4E93spA5cnYiux1FfWCp5T0Vi15OuYIWF6OBpaZbXpwsb9SfAGrRpncjcJMqVZNxt1LRia1eLBVzZmaAs8If5r1pn). The delays are attributed to a combination of factors, including the COVID-19 pandemic, manufacturing challenges with key first-of-a-kind components like the vacuum vessel and thermal shields, and an initial timeline that was deemed "too optimistic" [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHFhZ1yEceYqDXSbiiWscWWNsAbNdodzwx3AY_WkQlA5QEO04II-yDu0PfgRZDGCFJqfa6Y3W3I5g0wtzYhYR9iZrCLEqaIhIkmSnC94phVMH8dx-OckLS93cqycR9EjYdUL2oK99ZjIM4j2yQ=) [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHRwwXII-FrtYdY5-Wj4fIe8mVzjSR8nqqik-t71u8SeqBhFOCAU5k55_QGrtQ-gyBc0nf1wUrR9U9CUYwLG3zznXkOS_u74LoEYV02NONA54USBjLV40LBYMVQKCtLt5h0pCu0sks9DIXU8_sU) [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFPLamdfbmjkhhXUnPnd_byA-Vk8tWoPjD4viNzIeetGOf15NmJA1JsSzSvSgiuO7QdAPhrJElptGnpU-536EYbt8fIVASihFVixxqnMvMddUFfGyx6VwM4E93spA5cnYiux1FfWCp5T0Vi15OuYIWF6OBpaZbXpwsb9SfAGrRpncjcJMqVZNxt1LRia1eLBVzZmaAs8If5r1pn). The project's leadership has implemented a new strategy that consolidates assembly stages to create a more capable machine at the start of operations, rather than a staged approach [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFf3GQEmgy1Bu_JFMIj7sQ-vQsvJwhKf6bhfk1DczlP8NXaGKkh7nqoeSLjyMz9dh5PJSsoOSrKGW5A-uEM4o_wbj40R3vCFnoKbrcJRsGMaZovsO87Nt_l43GpXHhE9M50GidRVvEtNHpSUEwCZTS9psNa7O9962gnr8n7bewQgWWJf2IHJhRx8F8gdNMmiFd9CLaPOzJ1oY9s) [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHvhqrB79sg2Z8vk5-7Ga5vMmOfamzrVLqne2NIKmGNsf-xzn3wI9vZ5dqtsO6U6IAO8FKNy28XV8HHHsZOEkyZ4tnvB7M9Hh-baJsiXjFZnpjBom6HqeIG5RU5UxiI0dqZH5BBI9Vkr5U7QwYFCRvqV6O1Zz9Z0cY9ttuJXt4aOkt-jHaNRMEFhLfwIDFbS5KG8Wb1P5tMN5rybDGpow==). The estimated cost has also increased by approximately €5 billion [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFPLamdfbmjkhhXUnPnd_byA-Vk8tWoPjD4viNzIeetGOf15NmJA1JsSzSvSgiuO7QdAPhrJElptGnpU-536EYbt8fIVASihFVixxqnMvMddUFfGyx6VwM4E93spA5cnYiux1FfWCp5T0Vi15OuYIWF6OBpaZbXpwsb9SfAGrRpncjcJMqVZNxt1LRia1eLBVzZmaAs8If5r1pn).

While the publicly funded ITER project faces a longer road, the private fusion industry is experiencing accelerated growth and diversification. Numerous companies, backed by substantial private investment, are pursuing a variety of technological approaches to fusion.
*   **Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS)**, a spin-off from MIT, is developing compact tokamaks using high-temperature superconducting magnets. Their SPARC project aims to demonstrate net energy gain and is in the advanced stages of construction [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHDYbCG1iuHXw-E-p7N5K8vGWdSDUaEr-xKOBHOWsNCWby4fZXHpDOARDbptDEIyBhsEJTcYaY_UGf7DtbmEY34WvNAyhwEOSComL1n47fB6H-Gxp5SgM1fvVDMJxbCbrhcDV0yGhJwEvLladMOcwrz-HvPTpFJh_BQnhyAURfOZ4Pov2tvHcTegTeoUfKOpAzQh3ng14xKXG3XKLv1aIqMIyO1pkL0xUJlF8aJNg==).
*   **Helion**, which has a contract to provide fusion-generated electricity to Microsoft, is developing a pulsed non-ignition fusion system [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHDYbCG1iuHXw-E-p7N5K8vGWdSDUaEr-xKOBHOWsNCWby4fZXHpDOARDbptDEIyBhsEJTcYaY_UGf7DtbmEY34WvNAyhwEOSComL1n47fB6H-Gxp5SgM1fvVDMJxbCbrhcDV0yGhJwEvLladMOcwrz-HvPTpFJh_BQnhyAURfOZ4Pov2tvHcTegTeoUfKOpAzQh3ng14xKXG3XKLv1aIqMIyO1pkL0xUJlF8aJNg==).
*   **TAE Technologies** is focused on an advanced beam-driven field-reversed configuration approach using hydrogen-boron fuel [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGf_L4LDhbho2FdKyAREe8yzhhK_RY4AUR19jDMATQN6FlX5GbOlKiENohIMBoz7dUBd9JUr4zxvpmWvZfM9IZjvpCssh6yAL9DRnGpIwKkFHdTQun7vI2hEBql4jF2nq2geAXPBJsLxWaXMre-Xq_h0owej8ENLlO8xAQcCoAoU0m_Ubj8TSxQ6hcGg-l7aEOiEXkPs_L-Ek0=). Their fifth-generation reactor, "Norman," has sustained stable plasma at temperatures exceeding 75 million degrees Celsius [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGf_L4LDhbho2FdKyAREe8yzhhK_RY4AUR19jDMATQN6FlX5GbOlKiENohIMBoz7dUBd9JUr4zxvpmWvZfM9IZjvpCssh6yAL9DRnGpIwKkFHdTQun7vI2hEBql4jF2nq2geAXPBJsLxWaXMre-Xq_h0owej8ENLlO8xAQcCoAoU0m_Ubj8TSxQ6hcGg-l7aEOiEXkPs_L-Ek0=) [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHptTknDUUUQk-3pjEhGJCi4VLII1jQdGgW8c5A2PYNAVfQlHDOi65TqSA8ZxsL6PD10eL44DLaza0bZgLli6o3RUApG8MfkjjfvkiiaD4pntLDA0KEXu1fMXPKglsRY3DRYGyIdV7azHRqaE43r4O5TnGKSWbU0qz6T7dTFSZSyIjojmHNemh1drTSMqWDvKpGcuGmGfZIzBLmgXdJzf8Qfs6BwgwnxeUUavv23x6y9BgKkjVRwTPAYC5EA1EgS2wwfzizsPizkgdqlsJAbHDUDaXoylAf_ak=). They are now developing their sixth-generation machine, "Copernicus" [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHptTknDUUUQk-3pjEhGJCi4VLII1jQdGgW8c5A2PYNAVfQlHDOi65TqSA8ZxsL6PD10eL44DLaza0bZgLli6o3RUApG8MfkjjfvkiiaD4pntLDA0KEXu1fMXPKglsRY3DRYGyIdV7azHRqaE43r4O5TnGKSWbU0qz6T7dTFSZSyIjojmHNemh1drTSMqWDvKpGcuGmGfZIzBLmgXdJzf8Qfs6BwgwnxeUUavv23x6y9BgKkjVRwTPAYC5EA1EgS2wwfzizsPizkgdqlsJAbHDUDaXoylAf_ak=).
*   **General Fusion** is pursuing Magnetized Target Fusion (MTF) and is building a demonstration plant at the UK's Culham campus, with operations expected to begin in early 2027 [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQE7tlkcUye2IlGZf1TLfPyKWSDRN_rCc8h5_TocOdxlUB1y1V27yZBxkempw9l6KK-GmCLFtjh57ZhO0UFhN5s1JLGXhkMbIpsOY5Hq-IbDO7rVdHz0sKwdamMOJ7LE128Y-uFD2nRl4EkDKlU=) [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFeYBmbwpXilVDRbSIgNXDNRgG0HbUY48qFVd28IYXEtkOJN0K73skFdWO6_4nEDju1IMOfOJtn24O9FMsWKlqxTDXaIwSZn2DLytgFLBL7m7PnCtWMtygopp958yxY328eGV50PBrCW_Q=) [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGLCTMl2SOgLMkOrFjYfD3f-A4DN7nIlBiklK9fZSlekoq-MYE_nQyvQK_q0PBXj3Kzu9_s4sFaKjJExPdCv0FwuiX66V2arwGn--qvjOeYmfl4C7UW8H016zkLT6Qr58ECGwj_lqohhhFK7l_QFbwQ5br4TSJ4phAX3gysscVsQHge-v0mVhI09aJAkTQe7SoRLitG65C2DWxOQg==). Their "Lawson Machine 26" aims to achieve fusion conditions of over 100 million degrees Celsius by 2025 and progress towards scientific breakeven by 2026 [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFeYBmbwpXilVDRbSIgNXDNRgG0HbUY48qFVd28IYXEtkOJN0K73skFdWO6_4nEDju1IMOfOJtn24O9FMsWKlqxTDXaIwSZn2DLytgFLBL7m7PnCtWMtygopp958yxY328eGV50PBrCW_Q=) [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGEl2WIq7MzKF0HY-wc8q1gvRLTPy9zi9Sa7iyWqLTnSUP1Yh4vzo40V2W-8nc5nHjq0rFuMd317xe95NLK2Nx12RVwHQtH4zllJ8BhS84SX4VkuGzUG43jwuSDbimavPo8PjKFwAwKzg3vfaSPVgOg_DoOcl9CttSxjAF_z03GETDUBpJNGR6NiQd9nmwo6r4CPxAqEjzeW8QAwati2QnCFOlkw3IOardhlqcRhiAaQePS18SljJaElxBum0-9528yZxGd7MVeTPxFV2PwDbi_KTbACUFjV0jhGwrVEUs-hVbQzGK3K6zHGV6p9mIA3XqbsIEN8g==).
*   **Zap Energy** is developing a sheared-flow-stabilized Z-pinch technology, a more compact and lower-cost approach that does not require large magnetic coils [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHQ18Bxo1x-6qJ0zOGN5yiDYyGDOoySgSvTP-0p9QBl8yY-gRhi1WXCvGnk02it-3cXNntcPC8fYK6nuZmbDlm_vJQ1EhoRpprSHlF98KojwSavoG7ylaL5_t7o8dbQVNfrMOukbvyaHp6A54raf3Wr0LRBpBNQVOryiU0kbOOErQjEC3XtGCFtp4uhW6qW4tzXJ4t9icM1zl3r1OWUTrby) [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFNeaHyxX18iMCYOD3OEZ9KNTtk63QPKJCi-Or2wPFbryJfHffl99p3y48xUTXY5W1Ef6E9y9KyViL9KpRjdVHvu12-OeH9mPh_dsQwDEQYoyTmgRSpV1OSNqp8boKFkf1DpzyKADPwGFKBlg==) [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGmMpkaXdOL5b-4llXmWmV-EYI67gRAfvlC2MvrrGcqamafLpKomNp2uYA2M90SKpo7VRmg-56kUugjL6x7f0KAttMMuiuNnJOdStw2aqwLss475rA6MH2HH1Twlr8whPx9CGBaxoDEw5577TX2HpxkHwr3L0OYg_M8pSHLa3f7mxMWW9RettSSB6QKUJ3L6L0=). Their FuZE-Q device is operational and making progress in plasma performance [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHQ18Bxo1x-6qJ0zOGN5yiDYyGDOoySgSvTP-0p9QBl8yY-gRhi1WXCvGnk02it-3cXNntcPC8fYK6nuZmbDlm_vJQ1EhoRpprSHlF98KojwSavoG7ylaL5_t7o8dbQVNfrMOukbvyaHp6A54raf3Wr0LRBpBNQVOryiU0kbOOErQjEC3XtGCFtp4uhW6qW4tzXJ4t9icM1zl3r1OWUTrby) [source](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQE8szvNdgNpX-X0FmXHEcJ-mJY9CWvYEn9zyz2yKq-zAYboyE8WVZqo7l1zgNSi4gVqs8OjzN4Olr-jhJBc-wmAPRv4-x1rwSuAaP8nDxH6DJNxyWECo5KQAQ0JCuRtsZnfyy1u4de_ssmQU5-R).

In the nine decades since humans first produced fusion reactions, only a few fusion technologies have demonstrated the ability to make a thermal fusion plasma with electron temperatures hotter than 10 million degrees Celsius, roughly the temperature of the core of the sun. Zap Energy’s unique approach, known as a sheared-flow-stabilized Z pinch, has now joined those rarefied ranks, far exceeding this plasma temperature milestone in a device that is a fraction of the scale of other fusion systems.
A new research paper, published this month in Physical Review Letters, details measurements made on Zap Energy’s Fusion Z-pinch Experiment (FuZE) of 1-3 keV plasma electron temperatures — roughly the equivalent of 11 to 37 million degrees Celsius (20 to 66 million degrees Fahrenheit). Due to the electrons’ ability to rapidly cool a plasma, this feat is a key hurdle for fusion systems and FuZE is the simplest, smallest and lowest cost device to have achieved it. Zap’s technology offers the potential for a much shorter and more practical path to a commercial product capable of producing abundant, on-demand, carbon-free energy to the globe.
“These are meticulous, unequivocal measurements, yet made on a device of incredibly modest scale by traditional fusion standards,” describes Ben Levitt, VP of R&D at Zap. “We’ve still got a lot of work ahead of us, but our performance to date has advanced to a point that we can now stand shoulder to shoulder with some of the world’s pre-eminent fusion devices, but with great efficiency, and at a fraction of the complexity and cost.”
FuZE was originally funded for research at the University of Washington by the U.S. Department of Energy’s Advanced Research Projects Agency – Energy (ARPA-E). The device moved to Zap Energy’s dedicated R&D facilities in 2020, soon after the company was founded. The results in this paper were collected in 2022 in an ARPA-E funded collaboration with researchers from Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) and University of California, San Diego (UCSD), who spearheaded the development of the measurement system used for these results.
“Over many decades of controlled-fusion research, only a handful of fusion concepts have reached 1-keV electron temperature,” notes Scott Hsu Lead Fusion Coordinator at the DOE and former ARPA-E Program Director. “What this team has achieved here is remarkable and reinforces ARPA-E’s efforts to accelerate the development of commercial fusion energy.”
Hot soup
The first step to create the conditions for fusion is to generate a plasma – the energetic “fourth state of matter” where nuclei and electrons aren’t bound together into atoms but flow freely in a sub-atomic soup. Compressing and heating a plasma made of two forms of hydrogen called deuterium and tritium causes their nuclei to collide and fuse. When they do, fusion reactions give off roughly 10 million times more energy per ounce than burning the same amount of coal.
Such fusion reactions have been observed in the lab for decades in relatively small quantities. However, the great challenge is to create more output fusion energy from those reactions than the input energy required to initiate them.
Zap Energy’s technology is based on a simple plasma confinement scheme known as a Z pinch, where large electric currents are channeled through a thin filament of plasma. The conducting plasma generates its own electromagnetic fields, which both heats and compresses it. While Z-pinch fusion has been experimented with since the 1950’s, the approach has largely been stymied by how short-lived its plasmas are, a problem Zap has solved by applying a dynamic flow through the plasma, a process called sheared-flow stabilization.
“The dynamics are a wonderful balancing act of plasma physics,” explains Levitt. “As we climb to higher and higher plasma currents, we optimize the sweet spot where the temperature, density and lifetime of the Z pinch align to form a stable, high-performance fusing plasma.”
A healthy pinch
Fusion researchers measure plasma temperatures in units of electron-volts and can measure the temperature of the plasma’s ions (nuclei) and electrons separately. Since the ions are more than a thousand-fold heavier than the electrons, the two components of the plasma can heat and cool at different rates. Since the ions are what ultimately need to be heated to fusion temperatures, plasma physicists often worry about situations where cold electrons limit ion heating, like ice cubes in a hot soup. The electrons in the FuZE plasma, however, were shown to be as hot as the ions, indicating that the plasma is in a healthy thermal equilibrium.
Further, Zap’s detailed measurements show that electron temperatures and fusion neutron production peak simultaneously. As neutrons are a primary product of the fusing ions, these observations support the idea of a fusing plasma in thermal equilibrium.
“The results in this paper and further tests we’ve done since, all paint a good overall picture of a fusion plasma with room to scale toward energy gain,” says Uri Shumlak, co-founder and Chief Scientist at Zap Energy. “Working at higher currents we’re still seeing sheared flow extending the Z-pinch lifetimes long enough to produce very high temperatures and the associated neutron yields we’d predict from modeling.”
Gold standard measurements
The temperatures reported in the paper were measured by a team of outside collaborators from LLNL and UCSD skilled in a plasma measurement technique called Thomson scattering. To perform Thomson scattering, scientists use a very bright, very fast laser to fire a pulse of green light into the plasma, which scatters off of the electrons and provides information about their temperature and density.
“We’re especially grateful to the collaboration team for the work they did to help gather this data and refine a critical measurement technique for us,” notes Levitt. Informed by this collaboration’s measurements on hundreds of plasmas, Zap now routinely gathers Thomson scattering data on FuZE-Q, its latest-generation device.
No external magnets, compression or heating
Unlike the two mainstream fusion approaches that have been the focus of the majority of fusion research in recent decades, Zap’s technology does not require expensive and complex superconducting magnets or powerful lasers. “Zap tech is orders of magnitude less expensive and quicker to build than other devices, allowing us to iterate rapidly and produce the cheapest thermal fusion neutrons out there. Compelling innovation economics are vital to launching a commercial fusion product on a timescale that matters,” said Benj Conway, CEO and co-founder of Zap.
In 2022, the same time these results from FuZE were collected, Zap commissioned its next-generation device FuZE-Q. While early results from FuZE-Q are still forthcoming, the device has a power bank with ten times the stored energy as FuZE and capacity to scale to much higher temperatures and densities. Meanwhile, parallel development of power plant systems is also underway.
“We started Zap knowing we had a technology that was unique and outside the status quo, so definitively crossing this high electron temperature mark and seeing these results in a premier physics journal is major validation,” says Conway. “We’ve certainly got big challenges ahead, but we have all the ingredients to solve them.”
About Zap Energy
Zap Energy is building a low-cost, compact and scalable fusion energy platform that conﬁnes and compresses plasma without the need for expensive and complex magnetic coils. Zap’s sheared-flow-stabilized Z-pinch technology provides compelling fusion economics and requires orders of magnitude less capital than conventional approaches. Zap Energy has over one hundred team members in two facilities near Seattle and is backed by leading ﬁnancial and strategic investors. Visit Zap online at zapenergy.com.

Physical Review Letters
Method of Research
